citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$: every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $Q$ be a finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, second-countable smooth manifold without boundary, of dimension $n$. Its cotangent bundle is

$$T^*Q=\coprod_{q\in Q}T_q^*Q,\qquad \pi:T^*Q\to Q,\quad \pi(q,p)=q,$$

with the canonical smooth structure and induced cotangent charts supplied by the manifold construction in [[def-tautological-one-form-on-a-cotangent-bundle]]. The **tautological one-form** is $\theta_{(q,p)}(\xi)=p(d\pi_{(q,p)}\xi)$, and the **canonical cotangent two-form** is $\omega=-d\theta$. The exact theorem [[thm-the-canonical-cotangent-two-form-is-symplectic]] makes $(T^*Q,\omega)$ a symplectic manifold in the sense of [[def-symplectic-form-and-symplectic-manifold]]. We call this pair the **cotangent phase space** of $Q$.

In an induced chart $(q^1,\ldots,q^n,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$, $\theta=p_i\,dq^i$ and $\omega=dq^i\wedge dp_i$. A mathematical **observable** on this phase space means a smooth function $F:T^*Q\to\mathbb R$; this definition does not assert that a measurement has been performed or that every such function is physically measurable.

For an interpreted particle model, assign coordinates $q^i$ their declared units and assign the conjugate covector components $p_i$ units of action divided by the units of $q^i$. Thus $\theta$ and $\omega$ have action units, conventionally joule-seconds, and a bracket of quantities with units $[F]$ and $[G]$ has units $[F][G]/(\text{action})$. These are dimensional interpretations of the model, not additional mathematical premises. The use of $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$ is exactly the use in the smooth cotangent-bundle suppliers; no full Axiom of Choice is used.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$ and let $(M^{2n},\omega)$ be a smooth symplectic manifold. A finite family of smooth functions $\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_r$ defined on an open neighborhood $U\subseteq M$ is a **regular primary constraint family** on

$$C:=\{z\in U:\chi_1(z)=\cdots=\chi_r(z)=0\}$$

when $d\chi_1(z),\ldots,d\chi_r(z)$ are linearly independent at every $z\in C$. The regular-level theorem [[thm-a-regular-level-set-is-an-embedded-submanifold]] then gives $C$ its embedded-submanifold structure and $T_zC=\bigcap_a\ker d\chi_a(z)$. For functions $F,G$ on $U$, write $F\approx G$ when $F|_C=G|_C$; thus $F\approx0$ means that $F$ vanishes on $C$, without requiring it to vanish off $C$.

Given a smooth canonical Hamiltonian $H_c$ on $U$ and multiplier functions $u^a(t)$, the **total generator** is

$$H_T(t,z):=H_c(t,z)+\sum_{a=1}^r u^a(t)\chi_a(z).$$

The functions $u^a$ are independent parameter functions; the definition does not assert that their equations determine them. If $H_c$ is an energy and $\chi_a$ has units $[\chi_a]$, then $u^a$ has units energy divided by $[\chi_a]$, so every term in $H_T$ has the same units. A later constraint, if generated by consistency, is not declared primary by this definition.

Let $(P^{2n},\omega)$ be symplectic, and let $N=\{\chi_1=\cdots=\chi_r=0\}$ be a regular embedded level surface with $\{\chi_a,\chi_b\}=0$ on $N$. Then $\ker(\omega|_N)$ is exactly the rank-$r$ distribution spanned by the restricted Hamiltonian vector fields $X_{\chi_a}$. This distribution is involutive. Around every point of $N$, its leaves admit smooth Frobenius coordinates $(s^1,\ldots,s^r,y^1,\ldots,y^{2n-2r})$, and the local leaf space has a unique smooth closed nondegenerate two-form $\omega_{\mathrm{red}}$ whose pullback is $\omega|_N$. Thus regular first-class constraints yield a local symplectic quotient. No global orbit-space regularity follows from these hypotheses.

derivations.claim: The periodic quotient atlas makes $T^2$ a smooth manifold. By [F1], its cotangent form is $\omega=dx\wedge dp_x+dy\wedge dp_y$. The differential $dC=dp_x+a\,dp_y$ is nowhere zero, so $C^{-1}(0)$ is a regular embedded hypersurface. The canonical bracket is skew, hence $\{C,C\}=0$ and the single constraint is first class.
Contraction with $dx\wedge dp_x+dy\wedge dp_y$ gives $X_C=\partial_x+a\partial_y$. Integrating this constant vector field yields the stated flow and leaves momenta fixed.

Fix a starting point $(x_0,y_0)$ and any target first coordinate $u\in[0,1)$. For each $n\in\mathbb Z$, the flow parameter $s=n-x_0+u$ makes the first coordinate equal to $u$ modulo one and the second equal to $y_0+a(n-x_0+u)$ modulo one. The residues $na\bmod1$ are dense: for any integer $N\ge2$, divide $[0,1)$ into $N$ half-open intervals of length $1/N$. Two of the $N+1$ residues $0,a,\ldots,Na\bmod1$ lie in one interval, so for some nonzero integer $k$ and integer $r$ we have $0<\delta:=|ka-r|<1/N$; the strict lower bound follows from irrationality. Replacing $k$ by $-k$ if needed, $\delta$ is an integer multiple of $a$ modulo one. The residues $j\delta$ for $j=0,1,\ldots,\lfloor1/\delta\rfloor$ have gaps at most $\delta$ around the unit interval, so they form a $1/N$-net. Since $N$ is arbitrary, the multiples of $a$ are dense modulo one. Therefore the orbit is dense in the second coordinate for the chosen $u$; as $u$ was arbitrary, the flow orbit is dense in $T^2$.

The orbits through $(0,0,0,0)$ and $(0,1/2,0,0)$ are distinct: equality would require integers $n,k$ with $an+k=1/2$; if $n\ne0$ this would make $a$ rational, and if $n=0$ it would assert that an integer equals $1/2$. Both orbits are dense by step 3.1. Let $U$ be a saturated open subset of the constraint surface that meets the fixed-momentum torus. Its intersection with that torus is nonempty, open, and saturated. Its complement is closed and saturated; if nonempty, it contains a whole dense orbit and hence the whole torus. Therefore the intersection is the whole torus. Any quotient neighborhoods of the two distinct orbit classes have such preimages and therefore intersect, so the orbit space is non-Hausdorff. This does not contradict the local symplectic leaf spaces in [F3].

boundaries.reason: The theorem is conditional on the explicitly supplied smooth data; if no admissible datum exists, the universal implication is vacuous.
The statement has no zero-valued parameter boundary; it explicitly requires positive or nonzero data.
No separate one-dimensional or single-index boundary claim is made beyond the finite-index formulas stated.
The statement assumes the required regularity or invertibility and makes no conclusion at a degenerate point.
The theorem is local or pointwise and has no endpoint boundary case.
